verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “It hurts when I pee” and later confirms duration “Uh, six days.”
Patient reports “I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out” when urinating, consistent with malodorous urine.
Patient states “I've got, pain in my tummy… In my lower tummy… In the middle… Seven… Comes and goes,” supporting midline lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain, 7/10, intermittent.
Patient reports “I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots,” indicating hematuria with spots.

Patient denies fever (“No, not at all” to fever), lower back/loin pain (“you said you didn't have any lower back pain?” and “no loin pain as well”), vaginal discharge (“any vaginal discharge…?” Patient: “No, just the blood spot”), and reports passing water OK (“have you actually been able to pass water OK?” Patient: “Yes”), indicating no difficulty voiding.
First episode: Doctor asks “have you had these symptoms before?” Patient: “No. Never.” No recent triggers: to exercise/dehydration/regular intercourse, Patient answers “No.”
When asked about past problems, patient replies “I had IBS before.”
Doctor: “Do you take that regularly? … And it, do you take it three times a day? … Two hundred milligrams?” Patient answers “Yes” to both, confirming Mebeverine 200 mg TID.
On allergy query, patient states “Clindamycin.” Doctor confirms “You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.”
Patient states “I live with friends” and “I'm a support worker.”
Alcohol: Patient reports “One glass of wine a week.” Smoking: When asked “And do you smoke?” patient replies “No,” supporting never smoker in this context.

Doctor states “it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine,” i.e., cystitis. Symptoms in transcript: dysuria (“It hurts when I pee”), malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, hematuria with spots, afebrile by history (“No fever at all”), no flank/loin pain, and first episode (“have you had these symptoms before?…No. Never.”).
IBS is mentioned (“I had IBS before”) and Mebeverine use is detailed, but there is no explicit statement that IBS is currently stable on Mebeverine.
Medication allergy is explicitly stated: “Any allergies?… Clindamycin.” Doctor: “You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.”

Doctor: “we can treat this infection… with a course of antibiotics… It would just be for three days.” and “I can send a prescription through to your requested pharmacy… Knightsbridge, Practice… the antibiotics… will go through to that, pharmacy… pick them up as soon as you can, and start taking them,” supporting a 3‑day oral antibiotic e‑prescription to Knightsbridge Practice pharmacy to start ASAP.
Doctor advises “drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day” and “you can get some cranberry juice… and also some, sachets… which just help change the acidity of your urine.”
Doctor: “Have you got a thermometer at home?” Patient: “No.” Doctor: “It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature.”

Doctor gives safety‑net: “if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again.” and further “If… they're not resolving with the treatment. Or you keep getting a similar, problem, recurrently. Then it's important for us to talk to you in more detail about that.”
Mebeverine dose and frequency are confirmed, but there is no explicit instruction in the plan to continue Mebeverine for IBS.
